newsitem.title: SPAIN: Sevillana board recommends accepting Endesa offer.
newsitem.headline: Sevillana board recommends accepting Endesa offer.

text.p: The board of Spanish regional electricity company Sevillana has recommended it should accept a buy offer from state-owned Endesa for up to 75 percent of its capital, the company said on Friday.

"Endesa will launch a share buy offer of up to 75 percent of the social capital of Sevillana, whose board considers the offer friendly and recommends shareholders to accept it," Sevillana said in a statement.
The company said the aim of the operation was to increase the value of the companies ahead of the impending privatisation of Endesa, which is 66-percent state-owned.
This fitted in with the government's policy of creating large Spanish industrial groups in order to increase competitivity abroad.

"In the agreement, the signatories declare their intention of offering shares in Sevillana to business and financial institutions in Andalusia and Extremadura, especially savings banks, once the amicable buy offer is completed," it said.
Both companies wanted to promote regional development through investment in service infrastructure projects.
Endesa already holds a 39.4 percent stake in Sevillana.
